features.note: The plan bands are all individually legible, but the pass expectation is the HIERARCHY reading from the presets, and it does not. In lights-on-lobby the walls/floor sit at near-white; in lights-on-corridor the corridor walls sit at almost the same light-gray value; in lights-on/reference-match sala-3 the right auditorium wall is effectively pure white. Exterior -> lobby -> corridor -> auditorium is a single flat plateau of value instead of a four-step descent. Only the dark carpet separates corridor and auditorium floors, and that is a material, not a light.

Expectation is low-level aisle/exit/screen light revealing silhouettes. In lights-on-sala-3 and reference-match the room is lit from an untinted exterior wash: the right wall is blown to white, the left wall carries a green/teal cast, and the ceiling void is pure black. The two red seat-block masses read only because ambient hits their top faces flat -- no aisle-LED grazing, no screen spill, no rim. The two yellow aisle strips and the screen quad are the only emissive elements and they are visually inert. The auditorium is not a black hole; it is the opposite failure -- an over-exposed white box that no cinema rig would produce.

The red marquee and the Cinemex sign are genuinely focal in facade and grazing, with a believable specular sweep along the marquee's length -- the single best-lit element in the set. But the lobby behind the glass has no focal structure: in lights-on-lobby the tile floor is a uniform blown white with no gloss/clearcoat reflection, no ceiling-panel luminance, and no falloff toward the rear wall. The commercial-accent tier of the ladder is carried by three thumbnail-sized red panel strips and nothing else.

The lighting has NOT broken what earlier passes gated. eng-complete-network exposes every endpoint group plus the external schematic with no occlusion: green RS-485 trunks are traceable end to end, LoRaWAN reads as blue dashed, the IP chain reads as blue solid through ROUTER/FIREWALL -> INTERNET -> NIAGARA -> PC/TABLET/SMARTPHONE, and all labels hold contrast against the dark shell. eng-corridor and eng-sala-3 keep the green bus, the blue drops, TC300-04/07/08 labels and EXIT signs legible. Only demerit: at eng-neutral distance the fill is crushed low enough that TC300 labels lose legibility, against the spec's 'raise neutral fill slightly' note.

Neutral, grazing, reference-match and the engineering captures each remain legible in their intended state, and the architecture/engineering split is unambiguous (opaque massing vs 0.18 translucent shell with emissive media). Held just above threshold: the engineering state is darker than the spec's 'raise neutral fill slightly' asks, and the teal rim light tints the architecture roof planes and the sala-3 left wall a visible green rather than reading as an edge rim.

important_features.note: The 1.8 m figure at the entrance and the corridor figure sit correctly against the door bank and the 4.5 m public height; the UG67 and its two antennas on the corridor wall stay device-sized and are found by highlight/label, not by inflation.

This is the heart of the pass and it does not read. There is no luminance ladder: exterior, lobby, corridor and auditorium all sit inside roughly the same top-value band, driven by the exterior directional/ambient rig leaking through the whole interior at full strength. The lights-off pair proves it -- toggling house lights changes only a handful of thumbnail emissive strips (four under-marquee strips at grazing, three red lobby panels) while every wall, floor and ceiling value stays pixel-identical. corridor and sala-3 are byte-for-byte unchanged between lights-on and lights-off, so the two channels this pass OWNS (screen_emission, aisle_step_leds) produce no observable state change at all. The warm corridor ceiling fixtures exist -- they are visible as amber panels in eng-corridor -- but emit nothing in the architecture state.

eng-corridor and eng-complete-network show the RS-485 trunks running in ceiling containment and dropping vertically onto their TC300s, the UG67 antennas rising from the housing, and the bus/junction runs terminating on cabinets. Nothing floats.

defects: No luminance hierarchy. lights-on-lobby, lights-on-corridor and lights-on-sala-3 all render their walls in the same near-white to light-gray band. The corridor -- which the spec wants DIM -- has some of the brightest wall pixels in the entire set, brighter than most of the exterior shell.

Interior is over-exposed, not under-exposed. In reference-match and lights-on-sala-3 the right auditorium wall is crushed to white with zero shading gradient across a 25 m room. A cinema auditorium cannot have the brightest surface in the building.

The lights-on/lights-off pair does not prove the emission channels. lights-off-corridor and lights-off-sala-3 are visually identical to their lights-on twins -- the screen quad still glows, the yellow aisle strips still glow, every wall value is unchanged. The only real switching is four ~10 px under-marquee strips (grazing) and three red panel strips (lobby). The pass's two owned channels, screen_emission and aisle_step_leds, register no delta.

The scene is lit by one global wash, not by fixtures. There is no pool of light under any luminaire, no falloff from the emissive ceiling panels toward the rear lobby wall, no spill from the screen onto the auditorium floor. Every interior surface is flat-shaded by ambient plus the exterior directionals.

The teal rim light (0x00d4aa) is tinting large surfaces instead of rimming edges: in lights-on-neutral one auditorium roof plane reads solid green against the charcoal of the other; the sala-3 and grazing left walls carry the same green cast. It reads as a color bug, not as lighting.

grazing exposes smooth-plastic response. The white shell panels show one broad linear gradient and no highlight breakup, roll-off or micro-variation across the entire 60 m elevation; only the red marquee returns a believable specular sweep. The concrete apron is a single flat gray with no falloff away from the building.

Composition, facade preset: the building is compressed into a horizontal band occupying roughly the middle quarter of the frame, with ~40% dead black above and ~40% dead black below. The subject is not placed, it is stranded.

Composition, lobby preset: the camera is aimed into an empty corner. The frame is roughly half blown-white floor, and the upper third is the black roof-off void with an unexplained red marquee soffit intruding at the top-left.

Every interior preset opens onto a pure-black ceiling void (roof off) that occupies a large share of the frame -- corridor, sala-3, lobby. The value range of the images is bimodal (white walls / black void) with almost nothing in the mid-tones where the lighting story should live.
In lights-on-facade the ticket-kiosk screens behind the glazing read DARKER than in lights-off-facade (maroon/dark-blue on, bright blue off), which is an inverted or mis-wired emissive state.
corrections: Separate the interior from the exterior rig. Confine the sun/fill/rim DirectionalLights to the exterior shell and site (layers or a shadow/roof-aware mask) so they stop washing the lobby, corridor and auditorium interiors at full strength. The interior value must be produced by interior fixtures, not by leakage.

Build the four-tier ladder as explicit target values and verify them in the pixels: exterior/facade brightest, lobby/concessions one stop down, corridor two to three stops down, auditorium four to five stops down. In the current captures the corridor and auditorium must lose roughly 60-75% of their wall luminance.

Make the auditorium a dark room. Drop the sala interior ambient to near zero, let the ONLY light come from the aisle step LEDs, the exit signs and the screen. Raise the aisle-LED and screen emissive intensity so they carve the seat-block silhouettes and the floor step out of the darkness -- the seat masses must be revealed by that light, not by ambient.

Wire light_state=off to the actual emission channels this pass owns. On lights-off, screen_emission must go dark (or drop to standby), aisle_step_leds must go dark, the lobby/concession emissive ceiling panels must go dark, and the exterior marquee/under-canopy lights must go dark. The corridor and sala-3 pairs are currently identical images -- they must not be.

Give the lobby real fixture light: emissive ceiling panels that actually contribute luminance with visible falloff toward the rear wall, and enough gloss/clearcoat response in the tile that the floor returns a soft reflection instead of a flat blown white. Lower the base lobby exposure so the red commercial accents can sit ABOVE the wall value rather than below it.

Add corridor luminance from the warm ceiling strips that already exist in the model (they are visible in eng-corridor but emit nothing in the architecture state): make them emissive, keep the overall corridor value low, and let the green exit signs and red/blue accent LEDs be the brightest things in the frame.
Fix the teal rim light. Cut its intensity, restrict it to a rim direction that grazes silhouette edges, or drop the hue toward neutral so it stops tinting whole roof planes and interior walls green.
Reframe the facade preset: raise the camera target and shorten the distance (or narrow the FOV) so the building fills the vertical frame instead of sitting as a thin band between two black voids.

Reframe the lobby preset onto the actual subject (entrance line into the concession/ticketing axis) rather than into a bare corner, and pitch the camera down so the roof-off void stops taking the upper third of the frame.

Fill the interior ceiling void: with roof=off, cap the interior presets with a dark neutral soffit/ceiling plane so the frames are not half pure black, and so the emissive fixtures have a surface to read against.
Fix the inverted kiosk-screen emissive in the facade view: the screens must be brighter with light_state=on, not darker.

Break up the smooth-plastic shell response seen at grazing: add roughness/normal variation or panel-seam breakup to the white facade panels and the concrete apron so the highlight rolls off across the elevation instead of returning one flat linear gradient.
Raise the engineering-state neutral fill slightly, per the spec's engineering note, so the TC300 device labels stay legible at the eng-neutral camera distance without blooming the network media.
